<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="65.78.5.191" /></noinclude><section begin="par90" />{{GHGmargin-letter|90|g}}
(''b'') In the termination {{GHGheb|text=־ָ֫ תָה}} often used in poetry with feminines, viz. {{GHGheb|text=אֵימָ֫תָה|translate=terror}} (={{GHGheb|text=אֵימָה}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=15|verse=16}}; {{GHGheb|text=עֶזְרָ֫תָה|translate=help}} (={{GHGheb|text=עֶזְרָה}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=44|verse=27}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=63|verse=8|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=94|verse=17|hidebook=1}}; {{GHGheb|text=יְשׁוּעָ֫תָה|translate=salvation}} (={{GHGheb|text=יְשׁוּעָה}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=3|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=80|verse=3|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jon|chapter=2|verse=10}}; {{GHGheb|text=עַוְ֫לָתָה|translate=unrighteousness}} (={{GHGheb|text=עַוְלָה}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=28|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=10|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=125|verse=3}}; {{GHGheb|text=עֹלָ֫תָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=92|verse=16}} {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>th.}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=5|verse=16}}; {{GHGheb|text=צָרָ֫תָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=120|verse=1}}; {{GHGheb|text=עֵיפָ֫תָה|translate=darkness}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=10|verse=22}}; {{GHGheb|text=הַמְזִמָּ֫תָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=11|verse=15}} is corrupt, see the LXX and Commentaries. These cases are not to be taken as double feminine endings, since the loss of the tone on the final syllable could then hardly be explained, but they are further instances of an old accusative of direction or intention. In examples like {{GHGheb|text=עֶזְרָ֫תָה|translate=for help}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=44|verse=27}}) this is still quite apparent, but elsewhere it has become meaningless and is used merely for the sake of poetical emphasis.<ref>The form clings also to a few place-names, as {{GHGheb|text=גֻּדְגֹּ֫דָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=10|verse=7}}; {{GHGheb|text=שָׁלִ֫שָׁה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=9|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=4|verse=42}}; {{GHGheb|text=קְהֵלָ֫תָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=33|verse=22}} f.; {{GHGheb|text=יָטְבָּ֫תָה}} verse 33 f.; {{GHGheb|text=תִּמְנָ֫תָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=19|verse=43}}, &c.; {{GHGheb|text=אֶפְרָ֫תָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=5|verse=1}}, &c.]</ref>

{{GHGmargin-letter|90|h}}
This termination {{GHGheb|text=־ָה}} usually has reference to ''place'' (hence called {{GHGheb|text=־ָה|translate=locale}}<ref>Cf. Sarauw, ‘''Der hebr. Lokativ'',’ {{GHGcite|title={{abbr|ZA.|Zeitschrift für Assyriologie und verwandte Gebiete, ed. by C. Bezold. Lpz. 18S6 ff.}}}} 1907, p. 183 ff. He derives the {{GHGheb|text=־ָה}} from the adverbs {{GHGheb|text=שָׁ֫מָּה}}, {{GHGheb|text=אָ֫נָה}} and holds that it has nothing whatever to do with the old accusative.</ref>); sometimes, however, its use is extended to time, as in {{GHGheb|text=מִיָּמִים יָמִ֫ימָה|translate=from year to year}}. Its use in {{GHGheb|text=חָלִ֫ילָה}} properly ''ad profanum!=absit!'' is peculiar.

{{GHGmargin-letter|90|i}}
As the termination {{GHGheb|text=־ָה}} is almost always toneless (except in {{GHGheb|text=מִזְרְחָה|translate=constr. st.}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=4|verse=41}}; {{GHGheb|text=גִּתָּה}} and {{GHGheb|text=עִתָּה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=19|verse=13}}) it generally, as the above examples show, exercises no influence whatever upon the vowels of the word; in the ''constr. st.'' {{GHGheb|text=מִדְבַּ֫רָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=18|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=19|verse=15}}, and in the proper names {{GHGheb|text=גַּ֫תָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=2|verse=40}}, {{GHGheb|text=דַּ֫נָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=24|verse=6}} (so Baer; ed. Mant. and Ginsb. {{GHGheb|text=דַּ֫נָה}}), {{GHGheb|text=צְפַ֫תָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=14|verse=9}}, {{GHGheb|text=צָֽרְפַ֫תָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=17|verse=9}}, {{GHGheb|text=צָֽרְתַ֫נָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=4|verse=12}}, an ''ă'' is retained even in an open tone-syllable (cf., however, {{GHGheb|text=הֶ֫רָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=14|verse=10}}, {{GHGheb|text=פַּדֶּ֫נָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=28|verse=2}} from {{GHGheb|text=פַּדַּן}}, with modification of the ''a'' to ''è''; also {{GHGheb|text=כַּרְמֶ֫לָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=25|verse=5}} from {{GHGheb|text=כַּרְמֶל}}). In segholate forms, as a general rule, the {{GHGheb|text=־ָה|translate=local}} is joined to the already developed form of the ''absol. st.'', except that the helping-vowel before {{GHGheb|text=־ָה}} naturally becomes {{GHGterm|Š<sup>e</sup>wâ}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=בַּ֫יְתָה}}, {{GHGheb|text=הָאֹ֫הֱלָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=18|verse=6}}, &c.; {{GHGheb|text=הַיַּֽ֫עֲרָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=17|verse=15}}, {{GHGheb|text=הַשַֹּֽׁ֫עֲרָה}}<ref>So Qimḥi, and the Mant. ed. (Baer {{GHGheb|text=הַשַֹּׁ֫עְרָה}}), i.e. locative from {{GHGheb|text=שַׂ֫עַר}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=7|verse=20}}). The reading {{GHGheb|text=הַשַּֽׂעֲרָה}} (Opit., Ginsb.) implies a feminine in {{GHGheb|text=־ָה}}.</ref> {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=20|verse=16}}, &c., but also {{GHGheb|text=נַ֫חְלָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=34|verse=5}} (''constr. st.''; likewise to be read in the ''absolute'' in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=47|verse=19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=48|verse=28|hidebook=1}}) and {{GHGheb|text=שָֽׁעְרָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=28|verse=6}} (with ''Silluq''); cf. {{GHGheb|text=נֶ֫גְבָּה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=47|verse=19}} and {{GHGheb|text=גֹּ֫רְנָה}} (Baer, incorrectly, {{GHGheb|text=גֹּֽרְנָ֫ה}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=4|verse=12}} (both in {{GHGterm|pause}}).—In the case of feminines ending in {{GHGheb|text=־ָה}} the {{GHGheb|text=־ָה|translate=local}} is added to the original feminine ending {{GHGheb|text=־ָת}} ({{GHGpar|80|b}}), the ''ă'' of which (since it then stands in an open tone-syllable) is lengthened to ''ā'', e.g. {{GHGheb|text=תִּרְצָ֫תָה}}.—Moreover the termination {{GHGheb|text=־ָה}} is even weakened to {{GHGheb|text=־ֶה}} in {{GHGheb|text=נֹ֫בֶה|translate=to Nob}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=21|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=22|verse=9|hidebook=1}}; {{GHGheb|text=אָ֫נֶה|translate=whither}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=2|verse=36.42}} and {{GHGheb|text=דְּדָ֫נֶה|translate=to Dedan}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=25|verse=13}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|90|k}}
'''3.''' Of the three other terminations {{GHGheb|text=וּ}} may still be regarded as a survival of the old nominative ending. It occurs only in the middle<section end="par90" /><noinclude>
